record.paper_title: On Plane Geometric Spanners: A Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: Determine the smallest real number t such that every finite planar point set has dilation at most t when dilation is defined as the infimum, over all plane graphs with only finitely many added Steiner vertices, of the graph’s spanning ratio on all points of the set.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 18. What is the smallest value of t such that every finite set of points in the plane has dilation at most t? It is known that 1.00157 ≤ t ≤ 1.1247.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a finite set S of points in the Euclidean plane, define the dilation of S as follows. Consider all plane (i.e., crossing-free) straight-line graphs G whose vertex set consists of S together with finitely many additional Steiner points in the plane. For such a graph G, let
  d_G(p,q) = (length of a shortest path in G from p to q),
and define the spanning ratio of G on S by
  sr_S(G) = sup_{p ≠ q ∈ S}  d_G(p,q) / |pq|,
where |pq| denotes Euclidean distance. The dilation of S is then
  Δ(S) = inf_G sr_S(G),
where the infimum is taken over all such plane graphs G with finitely many Steiner points.

Determine the smallest real number t such that Δ(S) ≤ t for every finite set S of points in the plane. Equivalently, compute
  t* = sup_S Δ(S),
where the supremum is over all finite planar point sets S. (It is known that 1.00157 ≤ t* ≤ 1.1247; close the gap.)
artifact.status_search_result: The question of the optimal universal dilation constant for finite planar point sets (with finitely many Steiner points allowed) is a long-standing open problem in the geometric spanners literature. Known bounds remain roughly 1.00157 ≤ t* ≤ 1.1247, with works on related geometric-dilation variants (e.g., Dumitrescu–Gärtner–Rote; Ebbers-Baumann et al.; Mulzer; Klein) refining lower bounds slightly above π/2 in the related geometric-dilation setting, but no published resolution closing the gap for the graph-theoretic spanning-ratio version has been found.

status_evidence.title: Improved lower bound on the geometric dilation of point sets
status_evidence.snippet: Improves the lower bound on the dilation of point sets slightly above π/2.
status_evidence.claim: Lower-bound improvements exist for the related geometric dilation but the universal-constant problem for plane graphs with Steiner points is not closed.

status_evidence.title: Most Finite Point Sets in the Plane have Dilation > 1
status_evidence.snippet: For most finite point sets S there exists Δ(S) > 1 such that any finite plane graph containing S has dilation ≥ Δ(S).
status_evidence.claim: Research into the dilation constant continues; exact value remains undetermined.

status_evidence.title: The Geometric Dilation of Finite Point Sets
status_evidence.snippet: Upper bounds around 1.678 in the geometric-dilation setting; gaps between known lower and upper bounds remain.
status_evidence.claim: The optimal universal dilation constant is not yet pinned down.
